item.title: Comment on It’s later than you think by Schumpeter
item.description:
Tyler, respectfully, this is deeply retarded.

"Every faculty member should begin to write a detailed memo specifying the following: “What specific knowledge do I possess that AGI does not?"

Are you starting to lose the plot? It's not even that AGI is not here yet; it's that nobody has yet even presented a particularly concrete and well-defined theory of what it is. In the meantime you have some LLMs that are kind of fun and occasionally impressive in limited roles, but ultimately still just advanced forms of search + autocomplete. they're not Einstein or Darwin or Proust, and they're not even 1% of those people. and you also have a bunch of creepy snakeoil salesman like Altman who are trying to IPO and cash out and are "talking up their book" to inflate valuations to do so.

The idea that e.g. serious professors need to now justify their existence and courses because LLMs exist is brainworms-level insane. Please don't slip away on on us, we like you. Hold it together.

There’s a bit of a contradiction or inner tension in the article. If AGI is here and universities are cleaning out their teaching and administrative staff because AI does it better, then who are the students ?
What are they learning and for what purpose , since their chosen field is likely already taken over and mastered by AIs and the graduating student’s knowledge won’t cut in the work place. AGI implies accelerated self improvement of AI.

A world where most of the faculty has been replaced is also one where most workers are not needed at least for any kind of intellectual work and the need to instruct student inevitably steadily decreases towards zero.

item.title: Comment on It’s later than you think by Doug
item.description:
In my view, this fundamentally misses the key purpose of a university (and much about human nature). My small-c conservative view of a university/schooling is that it is a *commitment device*, designed to get students to care about learning. It fundamentally changes the long-term gains/short-term costs equation for people. This is hard to understand for some of the most bright, interested, disciplined, ambitious people in the world (e.g., Tyler Cowen, Bryan Caplan) who would learn on their own without being disciplined to do so. AGI does not really help solve this problem. As a matter of fact, LLMs and their projected futures are an iteration of libraries, the internet, and MOOCs, all of which have the potential for vast, free, human education. However, the limiting factor remains *individual discipline.* The social institution of a university/school has solved this problem in a way that none of these has. Look no further than COVID for the most recent example of why schooling/universities (and subsequently teachers/faculty) are not going anywhere soon. A corollary claim would be are most athletic coaches going to be replaced by AGI? I think not. In fact, I think quite the opposite.
